newsitem.title: Italy: Telecom Italia MD says '96 profits up. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia MD says '96 profits up. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: State controlled Telecom Italia's profits for all of 1996 will be the same or above the company's entire profits for 1995 net of mobile phones, managing director Francesco Chirichigno said on Wednesday.
(Company corrects headline and first paragraph to make clear it refers to profits for the whole year 1996, not just the first half).

Chirichigno, referring to results for first half 1996 at a meeting in the southern Italian town of Salerno, said: "It will be a half year reflecting what I promised to the shareholders' meeting and one which will point up successful management and cost reduction."
He added: "I had promised a profit net of the mobile phone business which would be equal to or above that of the entire 1995 year."
A Telecom Italia statement said later the latter comment referred to prospects for the whole of 1996 in respect to 1995.

Chirichigno said the figures for the first half of 1996, which are due to be approved by the board in the next few days, would also show an element of cost-cutting which would allow the group to be more competitive on the future global market.
Telecom Italia and the state-controlled mobile phone unit Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) were separated from each other half way through 1995.
Telecom Italia made a net profit of 1.745 trillion lire in 1995 on a turnover of 30.1 trillion.
